chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al- Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Hamzah ibn Ya'la, who linked it up through his chain, saying:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever is the enemy of his own self rather than the people, God will save him from the fear of the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.مَقَتَ: to be hostile or critical of

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of being critical of oneself rather than others?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith emphasizes *muhasabat al-nafs* (self-accountability) as a spiritual safeguard against the *faza'* (terror) of the Day of Resurrection, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical theology. By prioritizing self-criticism over judging others, the believer cultivates humility, ensuring divine protection from the overwhelming fear of reckoning. This reflects the Shia emphasis on internal purification as a precursor to external righteousness.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-54 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Hamzih ibn Ya’la who linked it up through documents to God’s Prophet (MGB) who said, “
Whoever is the enemy of his own self rather than the people will be saved by God from the fear of the Resurrection Day.”
